reviewer: ChatGPT original engineering author; NOT independent Pass C

rows.reason: Station mills cards to graveyards; Jester benefits only when its controller's spell or ability causes cards to be exiled from an opponent library.
rows.positive: With Underworld Breach and a zero-cost artifact, Station can fill a graveyard; Dauthi Voidwalker may replace opponent milling with exile and deserves rules-precise testing.
rows.cut_cost: Mox Opal supplies early metalcraft colored mana and is itself a zero-mana artifact that can be replayed or sacrificed to Station in Breach lines.
rules: The Jester triggers on opponent-library exile caused by controlled effects, not ordinary milling.
Station's activated ability mills three; the milling destination is ordinarily graveyard.
Dauthi Voidwalker's replacement effect may change the opponent card destination to exile; demonstrate whether this generates Jester permission.
A Station/Breach engine requires artifacts to sacrifice, mana to pay escape and sufficient graveyard cards.
The Madcap Jester and Dragon's Smile are authorized pending-release source exceptions, not certified current Commander legality.
rows.next: Run source-paid Station/Breach resource loop and Dauthi/Jester exile-causality adjudication.

rows.reason: Azula rewards low-mana instants and sorceries cast while she attacks. A seven-mana creature spellbounce engine does not replace Repeal's immediate double effect.
rows.positive: Hullbreaker can survive a contested stack as an uncounterable flash creature and bounce permanents upon additional spell casts.
rows.cut_cost: Repeal is a flexible instant that returns a legal target with mana value X and draws a card; Azula's copy may draw and bounce again with legal targets.
rules: Azula triggers on any spell cast while she is attacking, including instant Repeal.
Firebending adds red mana on attack but cannot itself pay all of Hullbreaker's seven-mana cost without other sources.
Azula copies a spell upon cast, not the resolved Repeal effect; copies need legal targets and can fizzle.
Hullbreaker's cast ability chooses returning spell or nonland permanent; it needs subsequent spell casts for repeat bounces.
Removing Repeal loses a cheap in-combat cantrip that assists combo sequencing.
rows.next: Compare in-combat real-target Repeal copies and source-paid late Horror spellchains.

rows.reason: Jeleva's attack ability casts exiled instant or sorcery spells, not creatures. Hullbreaker cannot be selected for her free-cast attack payoff.
rows.positive: Hullbreaker can interact on the stack later via flash and trigger bounces off cast spells when seven mana is accessible.
rows.cut_cost: Pyroblast answers blue spells or blue permanents for one red mana, protecting Jeleva's setup and ensuing high-value attack.
rules: Jeleva exiles from libraries when she enters using mana spent to cast her, not mana value.
Jeleva's attack permission is restricted to exiled instant or sorcery cards.
Hullbreaker is a creature and not a legal Jeleva free-cast target.
Pyroblast may target a spell or permanent and has the specified blue-dependent destruction/counter effect.
Hullbreaker's own uncounterability is not proof the main combo is safer than with low-cost stack interaction.
rows.next: Compare protection windows and seven-mana Horror availability against real opposing blue spells.

rows.reason: Eggman's villainous choices can deploy a Construct from hand, so Pit Automaton is on-theme, but a two-mana activated-ability mana creature may be low-impact compared with high-cost cheat targets.
rows.positive: Construct typing qualifies Automaton for the artifact cheat option; its ability-copy line may become relevant when actual exhaust targets and mana exist.
rows.cut_cost: Mox Opal offers zero-cost colored acceleration under metalcraft, speeding Eggman itself or his larger Constructs, Robots and Vehicles.
rules: Eggman asks an opponent to discard or permit a Construct, Robot or Vehicle card from hand onto battlefield.
Automaton is an artifact Construct and is eligible for that choice.
Automaton's restricted ability mana does not pay for Eggman's triggered choice.
Any exhaust-copy activation must pay its stated costs and obey tap restrictions.
Replacing Opal trades immediate colored mana for a narrower artifact/ability package whose activations need demonstration.
rows.next: Trace true printed Automaton ability and source-paid exhaust copy with target Eggman artifact package.

rows.reason: Hullbreaker can produce targeted opponent-facing crimes, which is a real Marchesa synergy, but it requires seven mana plus spells before it yields those crimes.
rows.positive: Each Hullbreaker spell-cast trigger targeting an opponent's permanent or spell can commit a crime and offer a Marchesa {1} selection if resource and trigger restrictions allow.
rows.cut_cost: Bowmasters is a two-mana flash card that can target an opponent or their permanent and punishes additional draw without waiting for seven mana.
rules: Marchesa crimes involve targeting opponents, their controlled permanents, or graveyard cards.
Hullbreaker triggers from its controller casting spells and may target spells or nonland permanents.
A Hullbreaker target on an opponent-owned object may count as a crime even if the triggered ability later fails to resolve.
Marchesa asks {1} after each qualifying crime trigger, so extra crimes are not automatically free cards.
Bowmasters trigger targets can be opponents or their controlled permanents and enable lower-curve crimes.
rows.next: Compare costed Hollowbreaker stacks, paid Marchesa triggers and Bowmasters flash/draw response turns.

rows.add: The Enigma Jewel // Locus of Enlightenment
rows.reason: Nekusar's core draw-punishment engines use triggered abilities, so Jewel's tap-for-restricted-activated-ability mana cannot directly cast wheel spells or pay triggered costs.
rows.positive: Jewel is a low-cost artifact whose ability activation mana can support actual activated artifacts; its crafted face can copy some activated abilities if the source supports the line.
rows.cut_cost: Offer is a one-blue-mana noncreature counterspell relevant to protecting a wheel, enchantment or win turn; opponent Treasures remain a real downside.
rules: Nekusar damage on opponent draw is a triggered ability, not an activated one.
Jewel enters tapped and produces mana restricted to activating abilities.
Jewel's restricted mana cannot cast a wheel or pay an ordinary nonactivated triggered payment.
Offer counters target noncreature spell and, on successful countering, creates two Treasures for that spell's controller.
Jewel crafting and Locus copy mechanics require separate real setup, never presumed from the front face's mana.
rows.next: Test source-listed paid activations, Jewel-to-crafted-face access and live noncreature protection counters.
